common_name: Plumetastic Pink Muhly Grass (Irvine Patented Late-Blooming Pink Muhly Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in full sun to partial shade and well-drained soil; Plumetastic flowers several weeks later than most pink muhly selections, so give it the longest possible run of warm fall weather before frost.

directions: Plumetastic is a Monrovia-introduced selection of pink muhly grass registered under the cultivar name 'Irvine,' chosen for flower plumes that open three to five weeks later than the common 'Regal Mist' selection, stretching the pink-to-purple fall display deeper into the season. Its fine, wiry foliage stays compact and tidy at roughly two to three feet before the bloom stalks rise another foot or more above the clump, making it well suited to containers, poolside beds, and slopes where a smaller-scale muhly is wanted. Like other forms of the species it thrives in lean, well-drained, even sandy soil and shrugs off heat and drought once established, but resents soggy winter sites. Cut the whole clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges to keep the form fresh for the next season's bloom.
sources: UC Davis Arboretum and Public Garden
